hero.subhead: The skill life-cycle manager for AI agents. Search, install, run, build, audit, and publish — one platform from spec to ship, without bolting six tools together.
hero.subheadStatic: The skill life-cycle manager for AI agents — search, install, build, publish, audit. One platform, every runtime.

why.pillar1Body: Skills live on a versioned, audited registry — not in Slack threads or random gists. Pull on demand from inside your agent via {{cmd}}.
why.pillar2Body: Describe the skill in plain English; {{cmd}} drafts a working SKILL.md you can iterate on, sandbox, and publish to the registry.
why.pillar2Proof: // ornn-build is itself a skill on the registry
why.pillar3Body: Platform-agnostic skill format with a sandbox playground (Node + Python) before you ship. NyxID-gated for anything that needs auth.

compare.subhead: A few things ORNN is often confused with, and what makes it different.
compare.row1UsSuffix: creates — you, your team, the world.
compare.row2UsSuffix: with a sandboxed runtime and audited, versioned releases.
compare.row3UsSuffix: — not Claude-locked. Skills travel with the agent that consumes them.
compare.row4Them: Not a runtime — execution happens in the agent.

install.body: Skills ship as plain markdown with manifest metadata — portable by design, with no glue code between runtimes. Today they pull into Claude Code; the format is open and agent-agnostic.

publish.body: You built something useful. Others need it too. Push to ORNN and it lives on the registry — versioned, audited, ready to pull into your agent.
publish.step2BodySuffix: (Node + Python). NyxID-gated for anything that needs auth.
publish.step3Body: One command. Versioned, audited, live on the registry.

footer.tagline: The end-to-end skill life-cycle manager for AI agents.

githubLink.intro: Point this skill at a folder in a public GitHub repo. Saving the link does not pull anything; click Sync afterwards to preview changes and publish a new version.
githubLink.urlHelp: Use the folder URL (the /tree/<ref>/<path> form). The skill's SKILL.md must be at the root of that folder. Default-branch and repo-root URLs work too.
githubLink.skipValidationHelp: GitHub-hosted skills don't always follow Ornn's package rules; tick this if you trust the upstream and want syncs to succeed even when the validator would reject the layout.
githubLink.saveBeforeSync: Save the URL change first, then sync.
githubLink.alreadyInSync: Already in sync — no changes to pull from GitHub.
githubLink.syncSuccess: Synced from GitHub — new version published.
githubLink.previewSubtitle: Apply this sync to publish v{{version}} of {{name}} from the linked GitHub source.
